sections.title: Code Example 1 — Re-ranking with sentence-transformers CrossEncoder
sections.body:
```python name=reranking_example1.py
# pip install sentence-transformers fastembed chromadb

from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
from fastembed import TextEmbedding
import chromadb

# ─── DOCUMENTS ───
corpus = [
    "The Python GIL prevents true parallelism in CPU-bound tasks",
    "Python multiprocessing module bypasses the GIL limitation",
    "asyncio in Python handles concurrent I/O operations efficiently",
    "Python threading is useful for I/O-bound concurrent tasks",
    "Rust programming language offers memory safety without GC",
    "Go language has goroutines for lightweight concurrency",
    "Java virtual threads are lightweight alternatives to OS threads",
    "Python subprocess runs external commands in separate processes",
    "Python concurrent.futures simplifies parallel task execution",
    "Node.js uses event loop for non-blocking I/O operations",
]

# ─── SETUP SEMANTIC RETRIEVAL ───
embed_model = TextEmbedding("BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")
client = chromadb.Client()
collection = client.create_collection("reranking_demo")

embeddings = [list(embed_model.embed([doc]))[0].tolist() for doc in corpus]
collection.add(
    documents=corpus,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    ids=[f"doc_{i}" for i in range(len(corpus))]
)

# ─── SETUP CROSS-ENCODER RE-RANKER ───
# ms-marco model is state-of-art for re-ranking (2026)
cross_encoder = CrossEncoder(
    "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2",
    max_length=512
)

# ─── TWO-STAGE RETRIEVAL + RE-RANKING ───
def retrieve_and_rerank(query: str, initial_k: int = 7, final_k: int = 3):
    print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print("=" * 65)
    
    # ── STAGE 1: Fast semantic retrieval ──
    query_emb = list(embed_model.embed([query]))[0].tolist()
    initial_results = collection.query(
        query_embeddings=[query_emb],
        n_results=initial_k,
        include=["documents", "distances"]
    )
    
    candidates = initial_results["documents"][0]
    initial_distances = initial_results["distances"][0]
    
    print(f"\n📋 Stage 1 — Initial Retrieval (top {initial_k}):")
    for i, (doc, dist) in enumerate(zip(candidates, initial_distances), 1):
        print(f"  {i}. [sem_sim={1-dist:.3f}] {doc[:60]}...")
    
    # ── STAGE 2: Cross-Encoder Re-ranking ──
    pairs = [[query, doc] for doc in candidates]
    rerank_scores = cross_encoder.predict(pairs)
    
    # Sort by re-ranking score
    reranked = sorted(
        zip(candidates, rerank_scores),
        key=lambda x: x[1],
        reverse=True
    )[:final_k]
    
    print(f"\n🏆 Stage 2 — Re-ranked Results (top {final_k}):")
    for rank, (doc, score) in enumerate(reranked, 1):
        print(f"  Rank {rank}: [rerank_score={score:.4f}] {doc}")
    print()

# ─── EXAMPLES ───
retrieve_and_rerank("Python concurrency and parallel processing", initial_k=7, final_k=3)
retrieve_and_rerank("handling multiple tasks simultaneously in programming", initial_k=7, final_k=3)
```

sections.body:
```python name=reranking_example2.py
# pip install langchain langchain-cohere langchain-chroma langchain-huggingface cohere

from langchain_cohere import CohereRerank
from langchain.retrievers import ContextualCompressionRetriever
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
from langchain_core.documents import Document
import os

# ─── DOCUMENTS ───
documents = [
    Document(page_content="RAG systems combine retrieval with language generation"),
    Document(page_content="Vector databases store embeddings for similarity search"),
    Document(page_content="Chunking strategies affect RAG system performance significantly"),
    Document(page_content="Embedding models convert text to numerical vector representations"),
    Document(page_content="LLM hallucination is reduced by grounding with retrieved context"),
    Document(page_content="Hybrid retrieval combines dense and sparse search methods"),
    Document(page_content="Re-ranking improves precision of initial retrieval results"),
    Document(page_content="Metadata filtering narrows search space before vector similarity"),
    Document(page_content="Query expansion adds related terms to improve recall"),
    Document(page_content="Contextual compression extracts relevant parts from documents"),
]

# ─── SETUP BASE RETRIEVER ───
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(documents, embeddings)
base_retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 8})

# ─── COHERE RE-RANKER ───
cohere_reranker = CohereRerank(
    cohere_api_key=os.environ["COHERE_API_KEY"],
    model="rerank-english-v3.0",  # Latest 2026 Cohere model
    top_n=3
)

# ─── COMPRESSION RETRIEVER WITH RE-RANKING ───
rerank_retriever = ContextualCompressionRetriever(
    base_compressor=cohere_reranker,
    base_retriever=base_retriever
)

# ─── SEARCH ───
def search_with_reranking(query: str):
    print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print("-" * 55)
    results = rerank_retriever.invoke(query)
    print(f"✅ Re-ranked Results ({len(results)}):\n")
    for i, doc in enumerate(results, 1):
        score = doc.metadata.get("relevance_score", "N/A")
        print(f"  [{i}] Score: {score} → {doc.page_content}\n")

search_with_reranking("how does RAG improve LLM accuracy")
search_with_reranking("techniques for better search retrieval precision")
```

# 🔷 TECHNIQUE 6: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance)

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**MMR** balances two goals:
1. **Relevance** — Retrieved documents should be relevant to the query
2. **Diversity** — Retrieved documents should NOT all be about the same sub-topic

**Formula:**
```
MMR = argmax [λ × sim(q, d) - (1-λ) × max sim(d, di)]
              ↑ Relevance       ↑ Redundancy penalty

λ = 1 → Pure relevance (no diversity)
λ = 0 → Maximum diversity
λ = 0.5 → Balanced
```

sections.body:
```python name=mmr_example1.py
# pip install langchain langchain-chroma langchain-huggingface

from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# ─── DOCUMENTS (intentionally overlapping topics) ───
documents = [
    # CNN cluster
    Document(page_content="Convolutional neural networks excel at image classification tasks"),
    Document(page_content="CNN architectures like ResNet achieve high accuracy on ImageNet"),
    Document(page_content="Deep convolutional networks learn hierarchical image features"),
    # NLP cluster
    Document(page_content="Transformer models revolutionized natural language understanding"),
    Document(page_content="BERT uses bidirectional transformers for language modeling"),
    # Reinforcement Learning cluster
    Document(page_content="Reinforcement learning trains agents through trial and error"),
    Document(page_content="Q-learning is a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm"),
    # Decision Trees cluster
    Document(page_content="Random forests combine multiple decision trees for better accuracy"),
    Document(page_content="Gradient boosting trees are powerful ensemble learning methods"),
]

embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(documents, embeddings)

# ─── COMPARE: Standard vs MMR Retrieval ───
query = "machine learning algorithms and neural networks"

# Standard similarity search (may return redundant results)
standard_retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity",
    search_kwargs={"k": 4}
)

# MMR retrieval (diverse results)

    search_type="mmr",
    search_kwargs={

    }
)

for i, doc in enumerate(standard_retriever.invoke(query), 1):
    print(f"  [{i}] {doc.page_content}")

print("\n🎯 MMR SEARCH (diverse results):")
for i, doc in enumerate(mmr_retriever.invoke(query), 1):
    print(f"  [{i}] {doc.page_content}")
```

sections.title: Code Example 2 — Custom MMR Implementation
sections.body:
```python name=mmr_example2.py
# pip install fastembed numpy scikit-learn

from fastembed import TextEmbedding
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

embed_model = TextEmbedding("BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")

# ─── CORPUS ───
corpus = [
    "Python is great for data science and machine learning",
    "Python NumPy provides efficient numerical computing",
    "Python Pandas helps with data manipulation and analysis",
    "JavaScript is essential for frontend web development",
    "React is a popular JavaScript UI component library",
    "Machine learning models predict outcomes from data patterns",
    "Deep learning uses multi-layer neural network architectures",
    "Data visualization helps communicate insights effectively",
]

# ─── EMBED ALL DOCS ───
corpus_embeddings = np.array(
    [list(embed_model.embed([doc]))[0] for doc in corpus]
)

# ─── MMR ALGORITHM ───
def mmr_search(
    query: str,
    k: int = 4,
    lambda_param: float = 0.5
) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    """
    Args:
        query: Search query
        k: Number of documents to return
        lambda_param: 0=max diversity, 1=max relevance
    """
    # Embed query
    query_emb = np.array(list(embed_model.embed([query]))[0]).reshape(1, -1)
    
    # Compute query-doc similarities
    query_sims = cosine_similarity(query_emb, corpus_embeddings)[0]
    
    selected = []
    remaining = list(range(len(corpus)))
    
    for _ in range(k):
        if not selected:
            # First: pick most relevant
            best_idx = np.argmax([query_sims[i] for i in remaining])
            chosen = remaining[best_idx]
        else:
            # MMR: balance relevance vs redundancy
            selected_embs = corpus_embeddings[selected]
            remaining_embs = corpus_embeddings[remaining]
            
            # Similarity to already selected documents
            inter_sims = cosine_similarity(remaining_embs, selected_embs).max(axis=1)
            
            # MMR scores
            mmr_scores = [
                lambda_param * query_sims[remaining[i]] 
                - (1 - lambda_param) * inter_sims[i]
                for i in range(len(remaining))
            ]
            chosen = remaining[np.argmax(mmr_scores)]
        
        selected.append(chosen)
        remaining.remove(chosen)
    
    return [(corpus[i], query_sims[i]) for i in selected]

# ─── TEST MMR WITH DIFFERENT LAMBDA VALUES ───
query = "Python programming and data science"

print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'\n")

for lambda_val in [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]:
    label = {0.0: "MAX DIVERSITY", 0.5: "BALANCED", 1.0: "MAX RELEVANCE"}
    print(f"\n🎯 MMR λ={lambda_val} ({label[lambda_val]}):")
    results = mmr_search(query, k=4, lambda_param=lambda_val)
    for rank, (doc, score) in enumerate(results, 1):
        print(f"  {rank}. [rel={score:.3f}] {doc}")
```

# 🔷 TECHNIQUE 7: HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings)

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**HyDE** generates a **hypothetical (fake) answer** to the query using an LLM, then uses that hypothetical answer as the search query instead of the original question.

> **Problem:** Query: "What causes diabetes?" → Short, sparse vector
> **HyDE Solution:** Generate a fake answer: "Diabetes is caused by insulin resistance..." → Dense, document-like vector → Better semantic match!

sections.title: Code Example 1 — HyDE with LangChain
sections.body:
```python name=hyde_example1.py
# pip install langchain langchain-openai langchain-chroma langchain-huggingface

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
from langchain_core.documents import Document
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
from langchain.retrievers import HypotheticalDocumentEmbedder

# ─── DOCUMENTS ───
documents = [
    Document(page_content="Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system attacks pancreatic beta cells, stopping insulin production. Patients require daily insulin injections."),
    Document(page_content="Type 2 diabetes develops when cells become resistant to insulin. It is linked to obesity, poor diet, and sedentary lifestyle."),
    Document(page_content="Gestational diabetes occurs during pregnancy due to hormonal changes affecting insulin sensitivity."),
    Document(page_content="Insulin is produced by beta cells in the pancreas and regulates blood glucose by allowing cells to absorb glucose."),
    Document(page_content="HbA1c test measures average blood sugar levels over the past 3 months and is used to diagnose diabetes."),
]

# ─── LLM SETUP ───
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)

# ─── EMBEDDINGS ───
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")

# ─── VECTOR STORE ───
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(documents, embeddings)

# ─── HyDE RETRIEVER ───
# LangChain's built-in HyDE embedder
hyde_embeddings = HypotheticalDocumentEmbedder.from_llm(
    llm=llm,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    prompt_key="web_search"  # Uses built-in template
)

# Custom HyDE approach for transparency
hyde_prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("""
You are an expert. Write a detailed factual paragraph that directly answers 
this question. Write only the answer paragraph, nothing else.

Question: {question}
Answer paragraph:
""")

hyde_chain = hyde_prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()

def hyde_search(query: str, k: int = 3):
    print(f"\n🔍 Original Query: '{query}'")
    print("=" * 65)
    
    # Generate hypothetical document
    hypothetical_doc = hyde_chain.invoke({"question": query})
    print(f"\n💭 Hypothetical Answer Generated by LLM:\n   {hypothetical_doc[:200]}...")
    
    # Search using hypothetical doc as query
    results = vectorstore.similarity_search(hypothetical_doc, k=k)
    
    print(f"\n📚 Retrieved Documents (via HyDE):\n")
    for i, doc in enumerate(results, 1):
        print(f"  [{i}] {doc.page_content}\n")

# ─── EXAMPLES ───
hyde_search("Why does the body stop producing insulin in some patients?")
hyde_search("How is blood sugar monitored over time in diabetic patients?")
```

# 🔷 TECHNIQUE 8: PARENT DOCUMENT RETRIEVAL

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**Parent Document Retrieval** splits documents into:
- **Small child chunks** → Used for precise semantic search (better embedding quality)
- **Large parent chunks** → Returned as actual context to LLM (more complete information)

> **Problem:** Large chunks → bad embeddings. Small chunks → incomplete context.
> **Solution:** Index small, return large!

sections.title: Code Example 1 — Parent Document Retriever with LangChain
sections.body:
```python name=parent_doc_example1.py
# pip install langchain langchain-chroma langchain-huggingface

from langchain.retrievers import ParentDocumentRetriever
from langchain.storage import InMemoryStore
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain_huggingface import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# ─── LONG DOCUMENTS ───
documents = [
    Document(
        page_content="""
        Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming every industry. 
        Machine learning, a subset of AI, enables computers to learn from data 
        without being explicitly programmed. Deep learning uses neural networks 
        with many layers to solve complex problems like image recognition 
        and natural language processing. AI applications include autonomous 
        vehicles, medical diagnosis, financial forecasting, and personalized 
        recommendations. The future of AI looks promising with emerging 
        technologies like quantum computing and neuromorphic chips.
        Companies like OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Anthropic are pushing 
        the boundaries of what AI can achieve. Ethical considerations 
        including bias, fairness, and transparency are crucial challenges.
        """,
        metadata={"source": "ai_overview.txt"}
    ),
    Document(
        page_content="""
        Climate change refers to long-term shifts in global temperatures 
        and weather patterns. While natural factors influence climate, 
        since the 19th century, human activities—especially burning fossil 
        fuels—have become the main driver. Carbon dioxide, methane, and 
        other greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere. The consequences 
        include rising sea levels, more frequent extreme weather events, 
        ecosystem disruption, and threats to food security. Solutions include 
        renewable energy adoption, carbon capture technologies, reforestation, 
        and international cooperation through agreements like the Paris Accord.
        Electric vehicles, solar panels, and wind turbines are key technologies 
        in the fight against climate change. Individual actions also matter.
        """,
        metadata={"source": "climate_change.txt"}
    ),
]

# ─── SPLITTER CONFIGURATION ───
parent_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=400,   # Large parent chunks
    chunk_overlap=50
)

child_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=100,   # Small child chunks for precise embedding
    chunk_overlap=20
)

# ─── SETUP ───
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(model_name="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")
vectorstore = Chroma(
    collection_name="child_chunks",
    embedding_function=embeddings
)
parent_store = InMemoryStore()  # Stores parent chunks

# ─── PARENT DOCUMENT RETRIEVER ───
retriever = ParentDocumentRetriever(
    vectorstore=vectorstore,
    docstore=parent_store,
    child_splitter=child_splitter,
    parent_splitter=parent_splitter,
)

# Add documents
retriever.add_documents(documents)

# ─── SEARCH ───
def parent_doc_search(query: str):
    print(f"\n🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print("-" * 55)
    
    results = retriever.invoke(query)
    print(f"📚 Retrieved {len(results)} parent chunks:\n")
    for i, doc in enumerate(results, 1):
        print(f"  [{i}] Source: {doc.metadata.get('source', 'N/A')}")
        print(f"       Content ({len(doc.page_content)} chars):")
        print(f"       {doc.page_content[:200]}...\n")

parent_doc_search("deep learning neural networks image recognition")
parent_doc_search("renewable energy solutions climate crisis")
```

# 🔷 TECHNIQUE 9: SELF-QUERY RETRIEVAL

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**Self-Query** uses an LLM to automatically parse a natural language query into:
1. **Semantic search query** (what to search)
2. **Metadata filter** (what conditions to apply)

> User says: "Find Python tutorials for beginners published in 2024"
> LLM extracts: query="Python tutorials" + filter={lang="Python", level="beginner", year=2024}

```
│                          │                                       │
│                          ▼                                       │
```

sections.title: Code Example — Self-Query with LangChain
sections.body:
```python name=self_query_example.py
# pip install langchain langchain-openai langchain-chroma lark

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain.retrievers.self_query.base import SelfQueryRetriever
from langchain.chains.query_constructor.base import AttributeInfo
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# ─── DOCUMENTS WITH RICH METADATA ───
documents = [
    Document(page_content="Introduction to Python variables, loops, and functions",
             metadata={"language": "python", "level": "beginner", "rating": 4.2, "year": 2024}),
    Document(page_content="Advanced Python decorators, metaclasses, and descriptors",
             metadata={"language": "python", "level": "advanced", "rating": 4.8, "year": 2024}),
    Document(page_content="JavaScript basics: variables, functions, DOM manipulation",
             metadata={"language": "javascript", "level": "beginner", "rating": 4.0, "year": 2023}),
    Document(page_content="React advanced hooks and performance optimization patterns",
             metadata={"language": "javascript", "level": "advanced", "rating": 4.9, "year": 2024}),
    Document(page_content="Python machine learning with scikit-learn and pandas",
             metadata={"language": "python", "level": "intermediate", "rating": 4.6, "year": 2024}),
    Document(page_content="TypeScript advanced generics and utility types",
             metadata={"language": "javascript", "level": "advanced", "rating": 4.7, "year": 2023}),
]

# ─── SETUP ───
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(documents, embeddings)
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)

# ─── DEFINE METADATA SCHEMA FOR SELF-QUERY ───
metadata_field_info = [
    AttributeInfo(
        name="language",
        description="Programming language of the tutorial: 'python' or 'javascript'",
        type="string"
    ),
    AttributeInfo(
        name="level",
        description="Difficulty level: 'beginner', 'intermediate', or 'advanced'",
        type="string"
    ),
    AttributeInfo(
        name="rating",
        description="User rating from 1 to 5",
        type="float"
    ),
    AttributeInfo(
        name="year",
        description="Publication year",
        type="integer"
    ),
]

# ─── SELF-QUERY RETRIEVER ───
self_query_retriever = SelfQueryRetriever.from_llm(
    llm=llm,
    vectorstore=vectorstore,
    document_contents="Programming tutorials and courses",
    metadata_field_info=metadata_field_info,
    verbose=True  # Shows what filters were extracted
)

# ─── NATURAL LANGUAGE QUERIES ───
def self_query_search(natural_query: str):
    print(f"\n🗣️  Natural Query: '{natural_query}'")
    print("-" * 60)
    results = self_query_retriever.invoke(natural_query)
    print(f"\n📊 Results ({len(results)} docs):\n")
    for doc in results:
        print(f"  ✅ {doc.page_content}")
        print(f"     {doc.metadata}\n")

# ─── EXAMPLES ───
# LLM auto-extracts filters!
self_query_search("Show me advanced Python tutorials with high ratings")
self_query_search("Find beginner JavaScript courses from 2023 or later")
self_query_search("What are the best-rated Python courses above 4.5 rating?")
```

# 🔷 TECHNIQUE 10: CONTEXTUAL COMPRESSION

sections.title: Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**Contextual Compression** retrieves full documents and then **compresses/extracts** only the relevant portions before passing to the LLM.

> **Problem:** Retrieved documents are long but only small portions are relevant
> **Solution:** Use LLM or extractive model to extract/compress only relevant parts
